transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-18
Start time: 16:30 PST
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luca Morales (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Aurora, Dir AI), Evan Locke (Aurora, Infra), Dr. Ben Park (Aurora, Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be fuzzy):
- Goal: agree POC timeline from kickoff to exec readout, confirm access gates, define success criteria and benchmarks, and identify blockers (networking/KMS/SOC2).
- Outcome: high-level sprint cadence agreed (3-week workstreams), access checklist to be sent, mid-point benchmark week target, exec readout scheduled, action items assigned.

Topics
- Kickoff tasks and access setup (VPC peering, service accounts, dataset delivery)
- Workload sizing and load profiles (RPS, tokens/session, concurrency targets)
- Benchmarks (latency p95, throughput, cost per 1k tokens, quality/regression gating)
- Milestones: kickoff, access complete, mid-point review, exec readout
- Security/compliance: SOC2, SAML, KMS/HSM, data residency

Transcript:
00:00 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'll do a quick roll call, um, and then Luca will walk through the benchmark plan. Priya, Evan, Ben, thanks for making time right before the holidays.
00:17 Priya Singh: Yep thanks Maya, appreciate it. We have a tight window, want to make sure we can get a clean readout for C-suite in January.
00:25 Maya Chen: Totally — high level goal today is to align on the POC sprint cadence, access gates, and what we measure at mid‑point vs exec. Luca, kick us off?
00:33 Luca Morales: Yeah, sure, I'll share my screen in a sec, but top level we usually run a 3 week sprint for this class of POC — week 0 kickoff + access, week 1 baseline and initial tuning, week 2 scale/batch/benchmark and then a week 3 readout prep — that's what I'm proposing. I'll call out exact artifacts, like the benchmark_spreadsheet link and the POC_access_checklist.docx.
01:02 Dr. Ben Park: Quick question, is week 0 counted in the 3 week window or is it separate? Because our exec calendar is tight.
01:10 Maya Chen: Good call, yeah we typically treat kickoff/access as a separate pre-sprint week, so the committed 3 weeks are focused on workload runs and benchmarks, but we can compress depending on access speed.
01:21 Priya Singh: We need the exec readout the week of Jan 20th ideally. Is that feasible?
01:29 Luca Morales: If we start kickoff the week of Dec 29th and access is done by Jan 2nd, then two full weeks of runs puts us mid-Jan for mid-point, and Jan 20th for exec readout is tight but doable if the access gate is not blocked.
01:44 Evan Locke: Network note — we'll need VPC peering or a secure egress proxy, and Aurora wants all egress IPs allowlisted, plus our security team requires KMS integration for any logs that leave the VPC.
01:58 Maya Chen: Noted — we'll put the IP ranges in the checklist. For KMS we support customer-managed keys in Redwood Private; for Hosted we can integrate with your KMS but need the KMS admin to approve a service principal.
02:15 Priya Singh: Our preference is Private, but we said we'd start with Dedicated if Private setup will slip. Any rough lead time differences?
02:25 Luca Morales: Private typically takes longer — provisioning and onboarding can be 2–4 weeks depending on approvals; Dedicated (cloud‑tenant reserved capacity) can be faster like 3–7 days once deps are confirmed. We should treat the POC as Dedicated unless security blocks it.
02:42 Priya Singh: Okay, we'll flag that as a risk.
02:46 Maya Chen: Let's capture that in the plan — decision point day 3 of kickoff whether to proceed Dedicated or escalate for Private.
02:55 Priya Singh: Works.
03:00 Luca Morales: On benchmarks — success criteria items we suggest: p95 latency below 450ms for the 8k context baseline, throughput of X sessions per second scaled to your peak, cost per 1k tokens below your current infra cost baseline, and no more than Y% quality regression on our eval prompts. We should pick the exact numbers together.
03:25 Dr. Ben Park: What's X and Y — we need concrete numbers for the exec slide.
03:29 Luca Morales: For example, X could be 12 concurrent completion requests sustained with 4k avg tokens per minute, and Y less than 5% drop on the golden prompt set. But those are placeholders; Priya, what are Aurora's expected per-user latency SLAs?
03:45 Priya Singh: For clinician-facing workflows we want 95% under 1s, ideally 500–700ms on typical queries. For batch background jobs latency isn't as critical.
03:55 Luca Morales: Good, so given that we'll tune for p95 under 700ms for clinician interactive flows, and use batching/quantization suggestions from Redwood Optimize for background batches.
04:08 Evan Locke: Also need to account for tokenization differences — our preprocessing expands tokens. We'll send a sample of 5k records so you can size properly.
04:18 Priya Singh: We'll anonymize the sample.
04:22 Maya Chen: Great. On the access checklist: items are — a) service account + API keys or VPC peering details; b) allowlist of IPs; c) KMS contact + key ARN if using CMK; d) SAML SSO contact for user provisioning to the console; e) test dataset and a small synthetic traffic generator. We'll send that checklist after this call.
04:45 Priya Singh: Anything about audit logs retention? We need 12 months for compliance.
04:50 Luca Morales: We can set retention on Redwood Console for up to 13 months for enterprise add-on, but in Private you can keep logs internally per policy. We'll flag retention options.
05:03 Maya Chen: Ok next piece is gating: Access complete is a hard gate — no benchmarking until VPC or API keys verified. Mid-point review will focus on baseline benchmarks (latency/throughput/cost) and quality checks. Exec readout will be a 30–45 minute session with slides covering ops, cost delta, and recommended rollout.
05:22 Dr. Ben Park: Who from Redwood presents at exec?
05:25 Maya Chen: Usually AE plus the SE — so Luca for technical results and me for outcomes and pricing. We can bring a solutions architect if needed.
05:33 Priya Singh: We'll invite CTO and VP Product.
05:36 Maya Chen: Great.
05:40 Luca Morales: I want to talk quickly about load profiles — can we agree on three profiles: 1) interactive clinicians: 12 rps, 4–6k token/session, 2) background batch: 200k tokens/minute with batched calls, 3) spike load: 30 rps for 5 minutes to simulate day peaks. We'll use those to configure batching, cache TTLs, and model variants.
06:03 Evan Locke: Seems reasonable, though our real traffic shows more variable token sizes. We'll provide a percentile distribution.
06:09 Priya Singh: Also, how do we measure quality? We're concerned about hallucinations in clinical notes.
06:15 Luca Morales: We'll run eval sets using your golden prompts and reference answers; measure exact-match and BLEU-ish metrics, but also human spot checks. We'll include cautionary gating: if hallucination rate above threshold, we stop and tune.
06:28 Priya Singh: Good. That gating is important.
06:31 Maya Chen: Next, what does success look like at exec? Often customers define two buckets: technical success (latency/throughput/cost thresholds met) and business success (NRR estimate, recommendation to rollout). Priya, what does Aurora want?
06:46 Priya Singh: At minimum, show comparable latency at 30–40% cost savings vs our current managed provider for the same model quality, and a clear migration path for private deployments.
06:57 Maya Chen: Noted. We'll include a cost model slide with assumptions.
07:02 Dr. Ben Park: Any concerns about PII? We'll only send de-id data, but our security team may request tracing disabled on tokens.
07:10 Luca Morales: We can scrub PII and advise on token sampling and KV cache settings; for Private we can guarantee no logs leave the VPC if configured. For hosted we can set log redaction and limited retention.
07:25 Evan Locke: We'll need a paper trail for that — any SOC2 artifacts?
07:28 Maya Chen: Yes, we'll attach the SOC2 report and security whitepaper in the checklist email.
07:35 Priya Singh: Timeline walk-through — can you lay out the exact dates?
07:40 Luca Morales: Proposed timeline: Dec 29–Jan 2: kickoff and access gating (week 0), Jan 5–Jan 12: baseline and first tuning runs (week 1), Jan 12–Jan 19: scale and mid-point benchmark (week 2), Jan 19–Jan 23: readout prep and exec session Jan 20th requested by Priya — we may shift a day but that's the rough map.
08:05 Priya Singh: The Jan 20th readout is preferred. If mid-point is Jan 12, we have one week to iterate which is tight but acceptable.
08:15 Maya Chen: We'll aim to keep mid-point by Jan 12 and set buffer days if needed.
08:19 Dr. Ben Park: What about regression detection — how often do you run evals during the POC?
08:25 Luca Morales: We run nightly automated evals on the golden set during the run weeks and a full manual check at mid‑point. If we see >3% drop on key metrics we pause and diagnose.
08:37 Priya Singh: Who owns that pause decision?
08:41 Luca Morales: Joint decision — Redwood SE recommends pause, Aurora stakeholder signs off to proceed after fixes. We'll document an escalation path.
08:51 Evan Locke: On networking — for VPC peering we require a ticket to our cloud infra team; how long to complete from Redwood's side?
08:58 Maya Chen: Once we get the peering details and the ticket, Redwood can provision the endpoint in 24–48 hours but approvals vary. That's why the allowlist and KMS contact should be prioritized.
09:09 Priya Singh: We'll put that as priority #1.
09:13 Maya Chen: Cool. On artifacts — we'll send: 1) access checklist, 2) benchmark plan spreadsheet with load profiles and metrics, 3) cost model template, 4) SOC2 and security whitepaper. Links will be in the follow-up email.
09:28 Priya Singh: Please include an explicit section on data residency and retention.
09:33 Luca Morales: Yep. We'll add a tab in the spreadsheet outlining retention options and costs.
09:38 Maya Chen: Let's capture decisions: kickoff week target Dec 29, access gate hard stop if not done by Jan 2, mid-point review Jan 12, exec readout Jan 20. Decision day 3 to choose Dedicated vs Private. Action owners noted.
09:55 Priya Singh: Sounds good. A couple of quick clarifying things — pricing, do you have a pilot rate or is it list?
10:03 Maya Chen: We'll propose a pilot pricing model for the POC in the follow-up: usually a timeboxed reserved capacity or usage cap for the duration to avoid surprise bills. We'll include an estimated cost table.
10:14 Dr. Ben Park: Any experimental features like quantized model variants we should be aware of?
10:18 Luca Morales: We'll test a quantized 4-bit runtime for cost runs; production default will be the full precision until we validate quality. We'll note model variants in the benchmark sheet.
10:28 Priya Singh: Good, want that explicitly in the readout.
10:31 Evan Locke: One more infra ask — will Redwood need IAM roles in our account for Private?
10:36 Luca Morales: For Private on-prem or VPC we may request a service principal for provisioner or a set of role ARNs; we'll specify minimum privileges in the checklist.
10:45 Maya Chen: Ok closing questions?
10:47 Priya Singh: None from me.
10:49 Dr. Ben Park: All set.
10:51 Maya Chen: Great — recap of next steps: we'll send the access checklist and the benchmark spreadsheet by Friday Dec 20. Customer to deliver sample dataset and security contact by Dec 22. Mid-point review week Jan 12. Exec readout tentatively Jan 20.
11:08 Priya Singh: Confirming those dates. Thanks everyone.
11:12 Maya Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the email and links.
11:15 Meeting ends.

Notes on transcription quality: automated transcript with occasional mis-heard technical terms (e.g., KV cache transcribed as K-V cash), speaker overlaps, and some timestamps approximate.

Referenced artifacts (will be sent):
- POC_access_checklist.docx (link included in follow-up)
- benchmark_spreadsheet.xlsx (load profiles, metrics, cost tab)
- Redwood_Security_Whitepaper.pdf

Explicit success criteria (captured in call and to be finalized):
- p95 latency for clinician interactive flows < 700ms
- throughput to support 12 concurrent interactive requests sustained
- cost per 1k tokens <= 60% of current provider (placeholder to be validated)
- quality regression <= 5% on golden eval prompts

End of transcript.
